name: rag_lwis2020
source: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks (Lewis et al., 2020, arXiv:2005.11401) — data/samples/rag_paper.pdf
note: Gold chunks are verbatim text fragments resolved against ingested chunks at load time (see researchrag/evaluation/dataset.py). Questions cover all 12 required classes, including cross-section and cross-page retrieval.

questions.question: Which Wikipedia dump did the authors use as the non-parametric knowledge source?
gold_chunks: we use the December 2018 dump
questions.gold_answer: The December 2018 Wikipedia dump

questions.question: How many documents does the Wikipedia index contain, and how were articles split?
gold_chunks: Each Wikipedia article is split into disjoint 100-word chunks, to make a total of 21M documents
questions.gold_answer: 21M documents, each article split into disjoint 100-word chunks

questions.question: Which pre-trained retriever initializes RAG's retriever and document index?
gold_chunks: We use a pre-trained bi-encoder from DPR to initialize our retriever
questions.gold_answer: The DPR (Dense Passage Retriever) bi-encoder

questions.question: What does the paper call the dense vector index of Wikipedia?
gold_chunks: We refer to the document index as the non-parametric memory
questions.gold_answer: The non-parametric memory

questions.question: What is 'Thorough Decoding' in the RAG-Sequence inference procedure?
gold_chunks: run an additional forward pass for each document z for which y does not appear in the beam, multiply generator probability with pη(z|x)
questions.gold_answer: Running an additional forward pass for each document whose beam did not contain a hypothesis, then summing marginals

questions.question: How is the input query combined with the retrieved document before generation?
gold_chunks: we simply concatenate them
questions.gold_answer: They are concatenated

questions.question: How are the retriever and generator trained, and what supervision signal do they receive?
gold_chunks: We jointly train the retriever and generator components without any direct supervision on what document should be retrieved
questions.gold_answer: Jointly end-to-end, minimizing negative marginal log-likelihood, with no direct supervision on retrieval

questions.question: Which training framework did the authors use for all RAG models and BART baselines?
gold_chunks: We train all RAG models and BART baselines using Fairseq
questions.gold_answer: Fairseq (with mixed precision)

questions.question: How much CPU memory does the full Wikipedia document index require, and what does compression reduce it to?
gold_chunks: requiring ∼100 GB of CPU memory for all of Wikipedia
reducing the CPU memory requirement to 36GB
questions.gold_answer: About 100 GB uncompressed, 36 GB after FAISS compression

questions.question: Which values of k were considered for training, and how was the test-time k chosen?
gold_chunks: We consider k ∈{5, 10} for training and set k for test time using dev data
questions.gold_answer: k in {5, 10} for training; test-time k chosen on dev data

questions.question: How many trainable parameters do the RAG models contain in total?
gold_chunks: making a total of 626M trainable
questions.gold_answer: 626M trainable parameters

questions.question: Compared to the DPR QA system, what does RAG demonstrate is unnecessary for state-of-the-art performance?
gold_chunks: neither a re-ranker nor extractive reader is necessary for state-of-the-art performance
questions.gold_answer: Neither a re-ranker nor an extractive reader

questions.question: On Jeopardy question generation, which model performs better on Q-BLEU-1, RAG-Token or RAG-Sequence, and by how much?
gold_chunks: RAG-Token performs better than RAG-Sequence on Jeopardy question generation, with both models outperforming BART on Q-BLEU-1
questions.gold_answer: RAG-Token (22.2 Q-BLEU-1 vs 21.4 for RAG-Sequence)

questions.question: What Exact Match score does RAG-Sequence achieve on Natural Questions in Table 1?
What Exact Match score does RAG-Token achieve on the standard TriviaQA test set?
questions.gold_answer: 55.2 EM (66.1 on the TQA-Wiki split)

questions.question: How many training examples does Natural Questions have according to Table 7?
gold_chunks: Natural Questions 79169 8758 3611

questions.question: Computing the top-k documents for a query amounts to which search problem, and how fast can it be approximated?
gold_chunks: is a Maximum Inner Product Search (MIPS) problem, which can be approximately solved in sub-linear time
questions.gold_answer: A Maximum Inner Product Search (MIPS) problem, approximable in sub-linear time

questions.question: According to Table 7, how many development examples does WebQuestions have?
gold_chunks: WebQuestions 3418 362 2033

questions.question: In the retrieval ablations of Table 6, on which task does the BM25 retriever perform best?
gold_chunks: For FEVER, BM25 performs best
questions.gold_answer: FEVER (entity-centric claims suit word-overlap retrieval)

questions.question: In Figure 2, which novel has a high document posterior for document 2 when generating answers for 'Hemingway'?
gold_chunks: The posterior for document 1 is high when generating
Document 2: ... artists of the 1920s ”Lost Generation” expatriate community. His debut novel, ”The Sun Also Rises”, was published in 1926.
questions.gold_answer: The Sun Also Rises

questions.question: Why did the authors keep the document encoder (and document index) fixed during RAG fine-tuning?
gold_chunks: Updating the document encoder BERTd during training is costly as it requires the document index to be periodically updated as REALM does during pre-training
questions.gold_answer: Updating it would require periodically rebuilding the document index (as REALM does in pre-training), which is costly, and they found it unnecessary

questions.question: In the null document experiment (Appendix F), what three ways were tried to model the null document logit, and what was the outcome?
gold_chunks: We explored modelling this null document logit by learning (i) a document embedding for the null document, (ii) a static learnt bias term, or (iii) a neural network to predict the logit
questions.gold_answer: A learnt document embedding, a static bias, or a neural network — none improved performance, so the mechanism was dropped for simplicity

questions.question: What are the two main components of a RAG model and what memory type does each correspond to?
gold_chunks: The retriever (Dense Passage Retriever [26], henceforth DPR) provides latent documents conditioned on the input, and the seq2seq model (BART [32]) then conditions on these latent documents
questions.gold_answer: A dense retriever (non-parametric memory) and a BART seq2seq generator (parametric memory)

questions.question: What hardware was used to train the RAG models?
gold_chunks: distributing training across 8, 32GB NVIDIA V100 GPUs
questions.gold_answer: 8x 32GB NVIDIA V100 GPUs (with mixed precision; single GPU is sufficient for inference)

questions.question: In the Jeopardy human evaluation, what fraction of pairwise comparisons did evaluators judge RAG more factual than BART?
gold_chunks: RAG was more factual in 42.7% of cases

questions.question: On FEVER, how often is RAG's top retrieved document from a gold evidence article, and how often is a gold article in the top 10?
gold_chunks: the top retrieved document is from a gold article in 71% of cases, and a gold article is present in the top 10 retrieved articles in 90% of cases
questions.gold_answer: 71% for top-1; 90% within top-10

questions.question: By how much does RAG-Sequence outperform BART on Open MS-MARCO NLG?
gold_chunks: RAG-Sequence outperforms BART on Open MS-MARCO NLG by 2.6 Bleu points and 2.6 Rouge-L points.
questions.gold_answer: 2.6 BLEU and 2.6 Rouge-L points

questions.question: What approximation does 'Fast Decoding' make to avoid extra forward passes in RAG-Sequence inference?
gold_chunks: we can make a further approximation that pθ(y|x, zi) ≈0 where y was not generated during beam search from x, zi
questions.gold_answer: It assumes the generator probability is ~0 for any hypothesis not in the beam for that document

questions.question: Which metric is used to evaluate the generated Jeopardy questions, and why was it chosen?
gold_chunks: we evaluate using the SQuAD-tuned Q-BLEU-1 metric
questions.gold_answer: SQuAD-tuned Q-BLEU-1, because it weights entities and correlates better with human judgment for question generation

questions.question: How many parameters does the BART generator used in RAG have?
gold_chunks: We use BART-large [32], a pre-trained seq2seq transformer [58] with 400M parameters
questions.gold_answer: 400M (BART-large)

questions.question: How did the authors demonstrate that RAG's knowledge can be updated at test time without retraining?
gold_chunks: we build an index using the DrQA [5] Wikipedia dump from December 2016 and compare outputs from RAG using this index
questions.gold_answer: Index hot-swapping: they swapped in an index built from the December 2016 DrQA Wikipedia dump and showed answers tracked the changed facts (e.g., 82 changed world leaders)

questions.question: What does Figure 1 of the paper illustrate?
gold_chunks: We combine a pre-trained retriever (Query Encoder + Document Index) with a pre-trained seq2seq model (Generator) and ﬁne-tune end-to-end
questions.gold_answer: The RAG architecture: a pre-trained retriever plus a pre-trained seq2seq generator, fine-tuned end-to-end with marginalization over retrieved documents
